newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico same-day Cetes rates up on election nerves.
newsitem.headline: Mexico same-day Cetes rates up on election nerves.

text.p: Mexico's same-day Cetes rates opened higher on Thursday, pressured by growing fears ahead of July 6 elections in which the ruling PRI is facing a pitched battle with the opposition.
"I think its a normal rebound because of pre-election jitters. Tomorrow it's going to be under more pressure, and on Monday, don't even talk about it," a Cetes analyst said.
The overnight Cetes rate was up 60 basis points in early trade, at 21.85 percent, in a move that traders said also responded to normal month-end liquidity pressures.

The uptick in rates was expected to accelerate as the election battle enters its closing stages. A poll this week suggested the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) may lose its 68-year-old majority in the Chamber of Deputies, which would give the opposition unprecedented influence over the annual budget.
Besides the lower house of Congress, the elections are also for a quarter of the Senate, six state governors and the mayor of Mexico City.
Analysts played down the influence of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on July 1-2, saying a rise in U.S. short-term rates by the Federal Reserve was not expected.
"The impact of the Fed is discounted, and in some ways it is helping ensure that the rise in rates is not as strong as it has been in the past," another market player said.
Bank paper was up 80 basis points at 22.95 percent.
Liquidity of 2.995 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
